reviewMode: Independent read-only source/fixture review; no Gradle, runtime test, browser, provider or network execution by reviewer.

findings.origin: Already identified by parent/author; independently confirmed in source review.
findings.behavior: Three stale positive leave/logout dialog callbacks now require the captured screen, exact transport, full federation authority revision and a live Activity before navigation or logout. The existing sensitive-command confirmation retains its form/screen/transport/revision fence.

sourceChecks.finding: run() captures expectedTransport and screen, rejects mismatched transport before worker execution and checks exact screen/transport/liveness before callbacks. All reviewed request closures use captured transport; old errors cannot clear the newly adopted api.

Only foreground VERIFIED adopts; flow.adopt() returns prepared transport/profile, then api and actor are installed without an intervening asynchronous boundary. heading advances screen, rejecting old buttons.

Explicit Cancel remains navigation-enabled during network work and cancels the exact flow. The corrective dialog guards close the delayed-positive path. No rollback of already committed business effects is claimed.

onStop pauses polling and adoption while retaining the bounded attempt for the external browser. Configuration retention carries the exact flow/transport; old destroyed-Activity posts are ignored. onStart resumes only the retained flow; non-configuration destruction cancels it.

A process-only weak rendezvous accepts the typed attempt callback. Re-arming cancels only the prior attempt; forget is identity-scoped. The Debug-only receiver handles both creation and new intents, rejects selectors/ClipData/URI grants, clears its Intent, and launches an explicit app component without forwarding caller extras or raw URI.
The host passes the original transport plus screen/liveness checks into the media screen; an old access error cannot clear a replacement account. The media runtime itself was not reaudited.
